subject: Cloud Computing
title: Durability vs. Availability
description: A short lesson to help you apply Durability vs. Availability.

hook.text: S3 promises 99.999999999% durability — eleven nines. That means losing one file in 10 billion per year.

buildup.text: Durability means data won't be lost. Availability means data can be accessed when you need it. They're different.

discovery.text: Cloud achieves durability by replicating data across multiple drives, servers, and often multiple data centers.

twist.text: High durability doesn't mean always accessible. S3 might be briefly unavailable while your data remains perfectly safe.

climax.text: Understanding the difference prevents panic. A brief outage doesn't mean data is lost — just temporarily unreachable.

punchline.text: Durability: will I lose it? Availability: can I reach it?

quiz.question: What is the difference between storage durability and availability?
options: Durability is about data not being lost; availability is about data being accessible
Durability means faster access speeds; availability means more storage space
They are the same thing with different names

details.summary: Durability measures the probability that data will not be lost over time. Availability measures how often data can be accessed when requested. Cloud storage offers extremely high durability through replication but availability varies by tier and configuration.
details.whyItMatters: Confusing durability with availability leads to poor architecture decisions. Data can be perfectly durable yet temporarily unavailable during an outage, and planning must account for both.
takeaways: Durability is about not losing data, availability is about access
S3 offers 11 nines of durability but lower availability SLAs
Multi-region replication improves both durability and availability

faq.question: What does 11 nines of durability mean?
faq.answer: It means 99.999999999 percent probability that an object will not be lost in a given year. Statistically, if you store 10 million objects, you might lose one every 10,000 years. This is achieved through replication across multiple facilities.

faq.question: Can data be durable but unavailable?
faq.answer: Yes. During a regional outage, your data may be safely stored on replicas but temporarily inaccessible. Multi-region replication or cross-region backup ensures both durability and availability even during regional failures.
